# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 15 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 15 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_015_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 15

**15:1** Now Annas the scribe came to Joseph and said to him, "Why have you not appeared in our assembly?" And Joseph said, "Because I was weary from my journey and rested the first day." And Annas turned and saw Mary with child.

**15:2** And he ran to the priest and said: "Joseph, for whom you gave testimony, has grievously transgressed." The priest said, "In what way?" And Annas said: "He has defiled the virgin whom he received from the temple of the Lord. He secretly consummated the marriage and has not revealed it to the children of Israel."

**15:3** And the priest said, "Has Joseph done this?" And Annas said, "Send servants, and you will find the virgin with child." The servants went and found it as he said, and they brought Mary and Joseph to the tribunal.

**15:4** And the priest said: "Mary, why have you done this? Why have you humbled your soul and forgotten the Lord your God — you who were brought up in the Holy of Holies and received food from the hand of an angel and heard the hymns and danced before them? Why have you done this?"

**15:5** But she wept bitterly, saying: "As the Lord God lives, I am pure before him, and I know not a man."

**15:6** And the priest said, "Joseph, why have you done this?" And Joseph said, "As the Lord my God lives, I am pure concerning her." The priest said: "Do not bear false witness, but speak the truth. You have stealthily consummated your marriage and not revealed it to the children of Israel, and you have not bowed your head under the mighty hand that your offspring might be blessed."

**15:7** And Joseph was silent.

---

## Translator's Note

The trial scene (15:3-7) follows the pattern of a formal legal accusation before a religious tribunal. Annas functions as the accuser/informer. Both Joseph and Mary swear the same oath formula ("As the Lord my/our God lives") and make essentially the same declaration ("I am pure"). Joseph's silence at 15:7 is not an admission of guilt but the response of one who has already said all that can be said and awaits divine vindication — which comes in the next chapter through the ordeal of the bitter water.
